stem: What was the immediate political result of the Contract with America in the 1994 elections?

options.text: Democrats kept control of both houses of Congress
options.misconception: The opposite happened — Republicans took both houses in 1994.

options.text: Republicans won control of both the House and the Senate
Republicans won the presidency for the first time since 1988
options.misconception: 1994 was a midterm election year; no presidential election took place.

options.text: The House and Senate both shifted to Democratic control
options.misconception: The opposite happened — both houses shifted to Republican control.

rationales.A: Background: the opposite happened — Republicans took both houses in 1994.
rationales.B: Background: Republicans won both houses in 1994 and had not controlled the House since 1954.
rationales.C: Background: 1994 was a midterm election year; no presidential election took place.
rationales.D: Background: the opposite happened — both houses shifted to Republican control.
rationales.general:
1. Read the passage for its promise: a Republican pledge to act in the first hundred days.
2. Background: voters handed Republicans both houses of Congress in 1994 — the House for the first time since 1954.
3. Background: the victory put President Clinton on the defensive with Congress for the rest of his presidency.
4. No president was elected in a midterm year, and the Democrats lost ground rather than gaining it.
Remember: 1994 was the Republican Revolution — both houses, at once.

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the Contract with America (1994). Post-1929 material is paraphrased, not quoted.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of the Contract with America, issued by House Republicans six weeks before the 1994 midterm elections: Led by Minority Leader Newt Gingrich, House Republicans promised a package of measures including tougher crime laws, welfare reform, tax cuts, and limits on Congress itself. They presented it as a pledge they would act on in the first hundred days of the new Congress.
